title: The Wrong Man
summary: Watchmaker Necati Aydın went to prison in 1989 for a jewellery shop robbery. Until the day he died he said, "I didn't do it." The films that could clear his name have been sitting in your shop for 37 years.

events.title: Robbery
events.body: Rıza's jewellery shop was robbed. The person who fled was limping.

intro.text: A bag in the "Never collected" cabinet: seven rolls of film. On it, Mrs Nermin's handwriting: "N. Aydın, 4 March 1989."
His name is in an old newspaper: watchmaker Necati Aydın, arrested on 5 March 1989 for a jewellery shop robbery.

intro.speaker: ayse
intro.text: My father said "I didn't do it" until the day he died. Nobody believed him. I was never sure either.

intro.speaker: ayse
intro.text: The robbery happened on Saturday 3 March, at 12:30. The person who ran was limping, and my father had an old leg injury. Two days later the police found a stolen necklace box in the back drawer of his shop.

intro.speaker: ayse
intro.text: My father said, "I was at the lake at that time, and Haluk was with me." But Uncle Haluk told the court, "I didn't see him that day."

people.name: Master Rıza
people.role: The jeweller across the street · the shop that was robbed

reels.title: The watchmaker's shop
reels.intro: The first film in the bag. On the label, Necati's handwriting: "Shop, February."

question.text: At 12:30, the time of the robbery, where was Necati?

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: That's what my father said for years. But Uncle Haluk said the opposite in court. One of them is lying.

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: But at 11:05 he hung "Closed" on the door. Would you close your shop just to sit alone? I don't know… maybe.

options.text: In the back street behind the jeweller's

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: I don't even want to think about it. But you're the one looking at the photos, not me. Maybe everyone was right.

outro.text: There's a second roll in the bag. The same handwriting on its label: "Lake, 3 March."

outro.speaker: ayse
outro.text: When you develop this roll, we'll see who was lying. My father, or Uncle Haluk.

question.truthNote: The lake photos on Reel 2 will show it.

hotspots.title: Necati Aydın
hotspots.body: Watchmaker. His shop sits right in the middle of the market; the sign is never dusty.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: My father painted that sign with his own hands. My mother used to tell me; I was a baby in her arms back then.

hotspots.title: The clocks are always right
hotspots.body: Every clock on the wall shows the same moment. You can trust the time in Necati's photos.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: My mother always said my father never left a clock wrong. "If a clock lies, so will a man," he used to say.

hotspots.title: Camera
hotspots.body: Necati loves photography; his camera sits on the counter, always within reach.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: I've never seen this camera. It vanished when my father was arrested. So he left it with Mrs Nermin, along with the films.

lines.text: The next morning Ayşe comes to the shop with a yellowed folder.
WATCHMAKER ROBS JEWELLER. On Saturday 3 March, around midday, Rıza's jewellery shop in our town was robbed. The arrested watchmaker, N. A., denies the charges. (6 March 1989)

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: My mother kept these clippings for years. I never had the courage to look.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: "Denies the charges," they wrote. As if keeping quiet were a crime too.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: You keep going with the photos. This time I'll read to the very end.

hotspots.title: Cem Demir
hotspots.body: Seventeen, Necati's apprentice. He loves the work; he looks up to his master.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: Cem. My father's apprentice. He left town after the trial; nobody knows where he went.

hotspots.title: Haluk Demir
hotspots.body: Police officer. Necati's childhood friend and Cem's older brother.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: Uncle Haluk used to visit us on every holiday. After the trial he never knocked on our door again.

hotspots.title: A new insurance sign
hotspots.body: A brand-new "Insured" sign in Master Rıza's window. Ayşe: "Maybe he robbed his own shop, to get the insurance money."

hotspots.title: Master Rıza
hotspots.body: The jeweller across the street. The shop that was robbed is his.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: A year after the robbery, Master Rıza closed his shop and moved to İzmir. Nobody knows what he got from the insurance.

hotspots.title: The shop opened
hotspots.body: The day of the robbery. Necati opens his shop as usual.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: 3 March. My father's last ordinary morning. He took this photo without knowing.

lines.text: In the evening the phone rings. Ayşe's voice is shaking.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: A letter fell out from among the clippings. My father wrote it from prison, when I was six.
My daughter, clocks don't lie. One day the clocks of that morning will speak too. On that day forgive me or don't, but know that I was at the lake.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: As a child I wouldn't have understood a word. But now we have the photos from that morning.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: The next frames are from the day of the robbery, aren't they? Look closely at the clocks.

hotspots.title: Cem left
hotspots.body: He said "My mother is ill" and asked for the day off.

hotspots.title: Red motorcycle
hotspots.body: Cem's motorcycle. There's no other red one in town.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: "My mother is ill"? My mother was neighbours with Cem's mother. She never mentioned her being ill that week.

hotspots.title: The shop closed
hotspots.body: Necati hung the "Closed" sign on the door.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: Closing the shop before noon on a Saturday isn't like my father at all. Either he had something very important to do, or someone called him away.

hotspots.title: Fishing rods in the car
hotspots.body: Haluk's car is at the door, fishing rods sticking out of the back window. They're going to the lake.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: The lake. For years my father said, "I was at the lake." If he really was there that day, the next roll will show it.

reels.title: Lake
reels.intro: The same handwriting on the label: "Lake, 3 March." The day of the robbery, around midday.

question.text: So why did Haluk tell the court "I didn't see him"?

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: Who? Not my father, clearly. He sank my father. Someone else, then.

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: Uncle Haluk was a policeman. Who could threaten him? But his voice really did sound frightened.

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: Three days later? A whole day they spent fishing? I'd like to believe that.

question.truthNote: Reels 5–6 will show it: he was protecting his brother, Cem.

outro.text: The label on the third roll in the bag: "Lake road."

outro.speaker: ayse
outro.text: My father photographed the way back too. Maybe they saw something on the road.

hotspots.title: They reached the lake
hotspots.body: The clock tower on the far shore shows 11:40. The town is 20 kilometres behind them.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: That clock tower is still standing. I drove past it last summer and never even noticed.

hotspots.title: Radio antenna
hotspots.body: Haluk is off duty today; no uniform. But there's a police radio antenna on the roof of his car.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: Uncle Haluk was always like that; even off duty he never let his radio out of reach.

hotspots.title: The first fish
hotspots.body: Necati has put his wristwatch next to the fish: 12:05. A watchmaker's joke.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: He did this with every fish. My mother used to say, "A watchmaker doesn't catch fish, he catches time."

lines.text: At lunchtime Ayşe comes to the shop, phone still in her hand.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: I called Uncle Haluk. For the first time in thirty-seven years.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: I said "the lake" and his voice changed. "Don't go digging up old things, girl," he said, and hung up.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: He wasn't angry at all. He sounded scared.

hotspots.title: Short shadows
hotspots.body: Necati's shadow is right at his feet. The sun is overhead: midday.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: The clock, the shadow, the tower… It's as if my father knew that one day someone would look at these photos.

hotspots.title: Necati was at the lake
hotspots.body: The watch beside the fish shows 12:30. At the moment of the robbery, Necati was 20 kilometres from town.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: 12:30… The exact time of the robbery. My father was telling the truth. Thirty-seven years later.

hotspots.title: Haluk was there too
hotspots.body: Haluk is holding Necati's fish, roaring with laughter. In court he said, "I didn't see him that day."

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: He swore an oath in court. In this photo he's holding my father's fish.

hotspots.title: The day's newspaper
hotspots.body: Next to the thermos, a newspaper dated 3 March 1989. The photo belongs to that day.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: A lawyer might say "the date can't be proven." But the newspaper and the watch both name the same day.

lines.text: Ayşe brings a photocopy of the case file. The corner of one page has been folded for years.
WITNESS STATEMENT · H. DEMİR · 12 April 1989. "I did not see the defendant Necati Aydın on 3 March. I was on duty all day."

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: "I was on duty," he said. But he was off that day; in the photos he's in plain clothes.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: Why would he lie? He was my father's closest friend.

hotspots.title: Still at the lake
hotspots.body: The tower shows 12:50. Twenty minutes after the robbery, the two of them are still on the shore.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: Twenty kilometres. You couldn't cover that road in twenty minutes, not even on a motorcycle.

hotspots.title: Arm in arm
hotspots.body: Necati set the camera on a log and used the timer to take a photo of them together.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: I'd love to hang this photo on the wall. But I can't look Uncle Haluk in the face.

hotspots.title: The last fish
hotspots.body: 13:00. Necati photographed the last fish with his watch, too.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: One o'clock. Half an hour after the robbery, they're still there. Now I'm sure.

reels.title: Lake road
reels.intro: On the label: "Lake road." Necati's second camera; the same day, between the lake and the town.

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: The only red motorcycle in town. He left saying "My mother is ill." His mother's house isn't on the lake road.

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: Could be. But that road only goes to the lake. What would a stranger be doing on the lake road?

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: At that time Uncle Haluk was with my father. And it's not his motorcycle; he has a car.

outro.text: The label on the fourth roll: "Shop, late afternoon."

outro.speaker: ayse
outro.text: A few hours after the robbery. Let's see who came back to the shop that day.

hotspots.title: The only road
hotspots.body: The sign: Lake 3 km, town 17 km. There's no other road between the lake and the town.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: This road is the only link to town. Everyone coming or going passes here.

hotspots.title: Empty road
hotspots.body: Around 12:10 the road is completely empty. Necati photographed the view.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: My father loved a view. But it's as if he were waiting for something.

hotspots.title: Red motorcycle
hotspots.body: A red motorcycle speeding towards town on the lake road. Necati's watch reads 12:18.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: A red motorcycle… What was it doing on the lake road? Where have I seen it before?

hotspots.title: The rider
hotspots.body: Enlarged: the rider has no helmet; dark, curly hair. Someone young.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: Curly hair… No. Let's not rush.

lines.text: Ayşe calls late at night.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: I found Cem online. He's a car mechanic in İzmir. Fifty-four, father of two.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: There's an old photo of him: standing in front of a red motorcycle. The caption says "My first love, 1987."

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: I'm not going to say anything. Not yet.

hotspots.title: Lost in thought
hotspots.body: Around 12:40. Haluk has put down his rod and is staring at the road.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: He isn't fishing. He's watching the road. He must have seen something.

hotspots.title: Police radio
hotspots.body: Haluk is listening to the police radio in the car. The robbery call must have come over this channel.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: He heard about the robbery right here, on the radio. And he didn't say a word to my father.

hotspots.title: Unaware
hotspots.body: Necati poses with his fish; he has no idea what's happening in town.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: At that moment my father looks like the happiest man in the world. Two days later he'll lose everything.

lines.text: Ayşe comes to the shop with a notebook, half of it scribbled over.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: I reached Master Rıza's daughter. Her father is still alive, in a care home in İzmir.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: His daughter said: "After that robbery my father never opened a shop again. He didn't get a penny from the insurance."

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: Not a penny? But there was an insurance sign in the window…

hotspots.title: To headquarters
hotspots.body: Haluk packs up, saying "I have to get to headquarters." It's 13:10.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: Half an hour after hearing the radio. Why didn't he go straight away? What was he thinking about for that half hour?

hotspots.title: A fresh track
hotspots.body: In the mud by the roadside, a thin, fresh tyre track. A motorcycle track.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: He photographed this too. Did my father suspect something?

hotspots.title: They returned to town
hotspots.body: The tower: 13:40. Police cars at the edge of town. Haluk dropped Necati here and drove to headquarters.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: This must be where my father first heard about the robbery. It never even crossed his mind that he'd be the suspect.

reels.title: Late afternoon
reels.intro: On the label: "Shop, late afternoon." A few hours after the robbery.

question.text: The robber was limping. Why is Cem limping?

options.text: He hurt himself jumping out of the window

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: Master Rıza said "the one who jumped fell." The same day, Cem's wrist is bandaged and he's dragging a foot…

options.text: He fell off his motorcycle, as he said

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: Maybe. But the motorcycle doesn't have a scratch. It's just muddy.

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: In the photos from the day before, he was running about. No, this is new.

outro.text: The label on the fifth roll: "Night light."

outro.speaker: ayse
outro.text: Night photos my father took for a competition. My mother used to talk about them; she never got to see them.

hotspots.title: Back at the shop
hotspots.body: The clocks on the wall show 16:00. Necati has reopened the shop.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: Three and a half hours after the robbery, my father calmly opens his shop. Is that how a guilty man behaves?

hotspots.title: Mud
hotspots.body: Cem's red motorcycle outside the shop. The wheels are muddy; the town's roads are paved.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: Mud… Is that mud from the lake road?

hotspots.title: Bandaged wrist
hotspots.body: Cem's left wrist is bandaged. He told Necati, "I fell off my motorcycle."

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: He fell… Could the robber have fallen too, jumping out of the window?

lines.text: Ayşe pulls a thick file out of her school bag.
STATEMENT · RIZA KARACA · 3 March 1989. "The person who jumped out of the back window fell, got up and ran off limping. I did not see his face."

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: My father had an old leg injury. Everyone looked at him.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: Nobody went looking for anyone else with a limp.

hotspots.title: Limping
hotspots.body: Cem drags his left foot as he carries a box.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: My father teases him and laughs. He didn't suspect a thing.

hotspots.title: The seal
hotspots.body: Master Rıza's shop is closed; a police seal on the shutter.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: Half the town must have been there. And my father was across the street, mending a watch.

hotspots.title: Uninsured
hotspots.body: Rıza's handwriting: the policy was due to start on 1 April. The insurer had put up the "Insured" sign. On the day of the robbery, the shop was uninsured.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: I suspected Master Rıza. That sign was just the insurer's advert. The man lost everything.

hotspots.title: Master Rıza
hotspots.body: In front of his shop, head in his hands. A man who has lost everything.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: For thirty years I blamed this man in my heart. I owe him an apology.

lines.text: Ayşe's phone rings. It's the care home.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: I spoke to Master Rıza. He's nearly ninety, but he remembers everything.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: "I never blamed Necati," he said. "The one who ran was light, quick on his feet. He was a boy."

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: A boy. In thirty-seven years, nobody ever asked him.

hotspots.title: He looks away
hotspots.body: Necati looks at the bandage and laughs. Cem has lowered his head and won't meet his eyes.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: He won't meet his eyes. I'm only noticing it now.

hotspots.title: Closing time
hotspots.body: The clocks show 18:00. Necati is closing the shop; Cem is still inside.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: Everyone is going home. Why isn't Cem?

hotspots.title: A shadow inside
hotspots.body: After closing, a shadow behind the window: someone behind the counter. Cem's height.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: What was he doing inside after closing?

reels.title: The drawer
reels.intro: On the label: "Night light." Necati photographed his shop at night for a photo competition.

options.text: He knew, and protected his brother

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: Then the lie in court makes sense too. But it means my father's friend did it knowingly.

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: If only. But he listened to the radio, he saw the motorcycle. Didn't he think at all?

options.text: He really believed Necati was guilty

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: Then why did he say "I didn't see him"? They were at the lake, together.

outro.text: The label on the sixth roll: "4 March, morning."

outro.speaker: ayse
outro.text: The morning after the robbery. One day before my father was arrested.

hotspots.title: Night shot
hotspots.body: The clock in the window shows 20:00. Necati is photographing his shop in the night light for the competition.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: My father really wanted to win this competition. My mother used to say, "He would have taken first prize."

hotspots.title: Long exposure
hotspots.body: The lamp is on and everything is sharp. Necati has set the camera on a tripod and is letting the light in for a long time.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: A long exposure… Anything that moves comes out blurred. My father knew that.

hotspots.title: A blurred shadow
hotspots.body: In a long exposure, anyone who moves comes out blurred: Cem, bent over the back drawer.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: Why is he blurred? He was moving. Putting something into the drawer, or taking something out.

lines.text: Ayşe takes a single page out of the case file; its edges are dark with fingerprints.
EXHIBIT 4 · Navy velvet necklace box. Found in the back drawer of the defendant's shop. 5 March 1989.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: I learned this photo by heart over the years. The box that convicted my father.

hotspots.title: Navy velvet
hotspots.body: The back drawer has been left ajar. Inside, the corner of a navy velvet box.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: The same box. The box from the case file. At 20:00 it was sitting in my father's drawer.

hotspots.title: Necati in the mirror
hotspots.body: Necati in the mirror: his eye at the viewfinder. He can't see the back drawer.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: My father is right in front of it, but he can't see. His eye is only on the light.

hotspots.title: Cem left
hotspots.body: 20:20. Cem picks up his helmet and leaves. His hands are empty.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: He leaves with empty hands. The box stayed in the drawer.

hotspots.title: The shop is locked
hotspots.body: 20:45. Necati locks the door. Only he and Cem have a key.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: They both had a key. Nobody else could have got in.

lines.text: Close to midnight, a message from Ayşe.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: I messaged Cem. "I found my father's photos from 1989," I said. Nothing else.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: It's been on "seen" for three hours. No reply.

hotspots.title: Competition photo
hotspots.body: The frame Necati picked for the competition. It was never sent in.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: What a beautiful photo. I'm going to frame it and hang it up, whatever happens.

hotspots.title: Unlocked
hotspots.body: The back drawer has no lock. Anyone in the shop could open it.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: Did the lawyer never ask about this? Anyone could have opened it.

hotspots.title: Rıza's stamp
hotspots.body: On the lid of the box, in gold leaf: "Rıza Kuyumculuk". The stolen box, here seven and a half hours after the robbery.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: There's no doubt now. Cem put the box there. Not my father.

reels.title: Haluk
reels.intro: On the label: "4 March, morning." The day after the robbery, one day before the arrest.

question.text: Why were these films never developed in 37 years?

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: Uncle Haluk said, "They always told me no." Someone hid these films on purpose.

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: He was arrested the next day. Served six years. Maybe… but would a man who lived for photography forget?

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: Then why is he still looking for them? He doesn't have the films. He never did.

outro.text: One last roll is left in the bag. On its label: "4 March, home."

outro.speaker: ayse
outro.text: The last photos my father took at home. The next morning they took him away.

hotspots.title: Haluk came
hotspots.body: 4 March, 08:00. Haluk arrives in uniform, before the shop opens.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: A Sunday morning, in uniform. If he wasn't on duty, why the uniform?

hotspots.title: Outside
hotspots.body: Haluk waves Cem outside. Necati photographs them through the glass.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: Why did my father take this through the glass? He must have been curious.

hotspots.title: An argument
hotspots.body: Haluk is jabbing a finger at Cem. You can't hear them, but their faces say everything.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: The older brother is scolding the younger one. Haluk knows.

lines.text: The shop bell rings. At the door, a tall old man; he takes off his hat.

lines.speaker: haluk
lines.text: Is this Mrs Nermin's shop? I left a film here, a long time ago.

lines.speaker: haluk
lines.text: I've asked now and then, for thirty years. They always said "no".
His eyes are on the cabinet at the back. He looks at it for a while. Then he leaves without asking for anything.

hotspots.title: Tears
hotspots.body: Cem is crying. Haluk has a hand on his shoulder.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: A seventeen-year-old boy. I can't even be angry; how strange.

hotspots.title: He looks in the drawer
hotspots.body: Haluk opens the back drawer and looks inside. Nobody told him where to look.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: He knows where to look. Without anyone telling him.

hotspots.title: He took nothing
hotspots.body: Haluk closes the drawer. Without touching the box.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: He could have taken it and thrown it away. But he left it there. In my father's drawer.

hotspots.title: A smile
hotspots.body: On his way out, Haluk touches Necati's shoulder and smiles. Cem took the photo.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: I will never forget that smile.

lines.text: At midnight Ayşe photographs the last pages of the case file and sends them.
SEARCH REPORT · 5 March 1989. Head of search team: Deputy Inspector H. Demir. A navy velvet necklace box was found in the back drawer.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: He led the search himself. Knowing exactly where the box was.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: The man who came to the shop today… That was Uncle Haluk, wasn't it?

hotspots.title: An ordinary morning
hotspots.body: 09:30. Necati is mending a watch, like every morning.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: He has no idea. The next morning they'll take him from this very bench.

hotspots.title: Cem is gone
hotspots.body: Cem's stool is empty. After that morning he never came back to the shop.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: He never gave a single statement during the whole trial. Nobody even asked him.

hotspots.title: Cem in the front seat
hotspots.body: Haluk's car drives away; Cem is in the front seat.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: He took his brother away. And the next day, my father.

reels.title: The last day
reels.intro: On the label: "4 March, home." The last roll in the bag.

question.text: The evidence table: who put the box in the drawer, and who covered it up?

options.text: Cem put it there, Haluk covered it up

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: The motorcycle at 12:18. The bandaged wrist. The blurred shadow bending over the drawer at night. Haluk checking that drawer the next morning without touching it. Everything points to the same place.

options.text: Cem put it there, nobody knew

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: The next morning Haluk went straight to that drawer. He led the search himself. He knew.

options.text: Haluk put it there and blamed Cem

reply.speaker: ayse
reply.text: At 12:30 Haluk was at the lake with my father. He couldn't have stolen the box or planted it. But he covered it up.

outro.text: Ayşe lays the photos out on the table. One by one, in order. This is the story that finally emerges:
3 March, lunchtime. Cem, who has gambling debts, gets into the jeweller's through the back window. Jumping out, he hurts his wrist.
He hides one of the stolen boxes in the back drawer of his master's shop, to collect it later.
At that time Haluk was at the lake with Necati. He heard about the robbery on the radio; on the road he had seen his brother's motorcycle. The next morning he learned the truth.
To protect his brother, he left the box where it was, led the search himself, and told the court he hadn't seen his friend.
Necati never found out who did it, to the day he died. You are the first to learn the truth.

hotspots.title: The Aydın family home
hotspots.body: 4 March, afternoon. Necati's house.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: This house… We sold it while my father was in prison. I don't even remember living here.

hotspots.title: Watchmaker's loupe
hotspots.body: Necati's repair table at home; a watchmaker's loupe on top.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: I have this loupe. The only thing I have left from my father.

hotspots.title: Baby Ayşe
hotspots.body: Ayşe's first steps. 4 March 1989.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: That's me. My first step. I never knew.

lines.text: For a long time Ayşe says nothing. She holds the photo in both hands.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: My mother used to say, "You took your first step towards your father's arms." I always thought she made it up.

hotspots.title: Her father
hotspots.body: Necati holds Ayşe in his arms at the repair table.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: The next morning they took him away. A father's last happy day.

hotspots.title: The clock at home
hotspots.body: 16:30. Necati is about to leave the house to drop off the films.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: His clocks are always right. Even at home.

hotspots.title: Your shop
hotspots.body: The sign reads "Karanlık Oda": the darkroom. Your shop, in 1989.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: This is… this is your shop! My father brought the films here.

hotspots.title: Seven rolls
hotspots.body: At the counter, a young Mrs Nermin takes in the seven rolls: "N. Aydın, 4 March 1989."

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: I've never seen Mrs Nermin this young. My father trusted her.

scene.eyebrow: TODAY · THE BOTTOM OF THE BAG
scene.title: A note

lines.text: At the bottom of the bag there's a folded, yellowed piece of paper. Mrs Nermin's handwriting.

On 6 March Mr Haluk came and asked for the films. I said "they came out ruined" and didn't give them to him. I couldn't take them to the court either; I was afraid. Every film in this cabinet is a debt.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: Mrs Nermin knew too. And she kept quiet for thirty-seven years.

lines.speaker: ayse
lines.text: She left the shop to you. Maybe so that you would pay the debt.

hotspots.title: The films were handed in
hotspots.body: Receipt No. 1147: N. Aydın, 7 rolls, 4 March 1989, 17:10. Ready for collection: 11 March.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: He was going to pick them up on 11 March. He was arrested on 5 March. He never came back.

hotspots.title: The last photo
hotspots.body: The only frame Necati took of himself: reflected in Karanlık Oda's window, camera in hand.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: He's smiling. He has no idea what tomorrow will bring.

hotspots.title: The last frame
hotspots.body: Light has leaked into the last frame of the roll. The rest isn't in the photos any more.

reaction.speaker: ayse
reaction.text: That's all of it. Now we know everything… don't we?

intro.speaker: ayse
intro.text: Uncle Haluk is seventy-one and retired. Cem is fifty-four, father of two. My father is gone.

finale.question: Who will you give the photos to?
finale.hint: There is no right answer. Ayşe will go with your decision.

options.detail: Apply to reopen the case, so that Necati's name is officially cleared.

ending.text: A week later, the town's only law office. The lawyer lays the photos out on the desk one by one.

ending.speaker: ayse
ending.text: Reopening the case could take months, she said. But my father's name will be officially cleared.
Two months later, a courthouse corridor. On the bench across from Ayşe sits a tall old man, hat on his knees.

ending.speaker: haluk
ending.text: For thirty-seven years, every morning, I thought about that drawer. He was my brother. I thought I had saved him.

ending.speaker: haluk
ending.text: Not Necati… I was saving myself. And not even that, really.

ending.speaker: ayse
ending.text: My father never blamed you, you know. Until he died he said, "Haluk must know something."
Haluk bows his head. He seems about to say something, but can't.
At the end of the corridor, Cem appears. He came from İzmir on the first bus, of his own accord. He sits down next to his brother and, for the first time, looks Ayşe in the face.
A courthouse corridor. The case of Necati Aydın has been reopened.

ending.speaker: ayse
ending.text: If my father could see this… Maybe he does.

options.detail: Let her know her father was innocent; let no one else know.

ending.text: Ayşe has the competition photo framed. She hangs it on her wall, next to her father's portrait.

ending.speaker: ayse
ending.text: No one will know. But I know. My father didn't do it.
One evening the shop bell rings. At the door, that old man again. This time he doesn't ask about the films.

ending.speaker: haluk
ending.text: Necati's daughter… does she know?
You nod. Haluk is silent for a long time. Then he takes a worn photo from his pocket and lays it on the counter: the lakeshore, two young men, arm in arm.

ending.speaker: haluk
ending.text: Give it to her. I have no right to keep it.
A week later, an envelope has been slipped under Ayşe's door. Inside, a single line.
I'm sorry. — C.
Ayşe's house. Two photos on the wall: the competition frame, and the two friends at the lake.

ending.speaker: ayse
ending.text: Sometimes knowing the truth is enough. Sometimes it isn't. Today it is.

epilogue.text: That night you're alone in the shop. No sound but the ticking of the clocks.
Mrs Nermin's note is still in your pocket: "Every film in this cabinet is a debt."
Where the bag used to be, you stick a small label in your own handwriting: "N. Aydın · collected."
There are dozens more bags on the shelf; each one is someone else's story. One label catches your eye: "Room 214, July 1979."
